description: Opens QuickDock, the compact DeepSeek Harness UI, in a VS Code tab.
config.title: DSH Dock
config.port.title: QuickDock port
config.port.description:
Loopback port of the QuickDock listener that the `dsh-quickdock` DSH plugin binds on `127.0.0.1`.

It must match **DSH → Settings → QuickDock → Connection** (default `47910`). Set it here when you moved the port there; when this setting is left at its default and `#dshVsdock.followQuickDockConfig#` is on, the extension reads the port from QuickDock's own `config.json` instead.
config.follow.title: Follow QuickDock's config.json
config.follow.description: When `#dshVsdock.port#` has not been set explicitly, read the port from QuickDock's configuration (`LOCALAPPDATA/dsh-quickdock/config.json`, or the `DSH_QUICKDOCK_STATE_DIR` folder). Turn this off to pin the extension to the setting alone.
config.statusBar.title: Show the status bar item
config.statusBar.description: Show whether QuickDock is reachable, and open the dock from the status bar.
config.mcp.title: Serve editor tools over MCP
config.mcp.description: Run a loopback MCP server that exposes read-only editor tools (diagnostics, symbols, selection, file reads) and register it with QuickDock for the open workspace folders. QuickDock forwards it to DSH's workspace-scoped MCP bridge, so only sessions inside those folders mount the tools; the dock's own title bar carries the switch. Enabling this setting is the pairing consent.
config.mcpPort.title: MCP port
config.mcpPort.description: Preferred loopback port for the editor's MCP server. A window that finds it taken uses a free port instead: the pairing carries the real URL, so no two windows collide.
config.review.title: Open a diff when DSH changes or creates a file
config.review.description: Open a diff for each file **DSH's own file tools** change. DSH reports every write it makes through the dock as it happens, so only the agent's edits get a tab - a Gradle, Maven or npm build running next to the editor writes to the disk directly and is never reported. The tab never takes focus, and generated folders, binaries and `#dshVsdock.reviewIgnore#` globs are skipped. Needs a QuickDock build that serves the `file-events` feed (`dsh-quickdock` 0.6+).
config.reviewIgnore.title: Paths that never open a review diff
config.reviewIgnore.description:
Globs for paths to leave out of automatic diffs, on top of the built-in list (`node_modules`, `out`, `dist`, `build`, `.gradle`, `target`, …) and the binary check.

A pattern without a `/` matches at any depth, and naming a directory covers everything below it:

```
generated/**
*.log
**/*.generated.ts
```
config.dshCommand.title: dsh command
config.dshCommand.description: The command **Start DSH** runs in a terminal. `dsh` uses whatever is on `PATH`; set an absolute path (for example `C:\Tools\dsh.cmd`) when several installs exist or `PATH` does not have it.
config.dshProfile.title: DSH profile
config.dshProfile.description: The profile passed as `dsh --profile <name>` (for example `desktop` or `web`). Empty lets DSH pick its default, and **Start DSH** offers a picker when profiles exist under `~/.dsh/profiles`.
config.dshArgs.title: Extra dsh arguments
config.dshArgs.description: Appended to the launch line verbatim, after the profile flag (for example `--port 8080`).
config.mcpWriteTools.title: Let DSH's agent change the editor
config.mcpWriteTools.description: Add the tools that change state: `vscode_apply_edit` (an unsaved edit plus a review diff), `vscode_save_file`, `vscode_run_task`, `vscode_terminal_run` and `vscode_start_debug`. Off by default: they reach past the DSH sandbox into your editor and terminal.
